DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 84 s. 29 June 2021 HON. AZUCENA CHAPMAN Sanggunian Bayan Member Municipality of Ivisan, Capiz panublihanone@qmail.com Dear SB Member Chapman: 2021 This has reference to your Email dated 13 April 2021 in reply to the opinion dated 10 February 2021. The Department addressed the request for opinion by providing the basic legal bases found under the Local Government Code on parliamentary procedures to which the letter-sender must rely on. Explicitly explained is that other than that which can be gleaned from the Internal Rules of Procedures of the sanggunian and the Local Government Code, answers to issues on whether or not parliamentary procedure is followed by the proceedings in the sanggunian are to be derived from the published materials authored by learned experts on the subject, precisely because the matter is already beyond the opinion-rendition authority of this Department. This is beyond the fact that the Department is also not a privy as to what has been agreed upon by the members of the Sanggunian on how to go about its own parliamentary procedures and as to what is contained in its own Internal Rules of Procedures. Now, therefore, to directly address the statements and/or inquiry in your email-reply. We quote what has been written: "Your letter expresses your hope that I have been guided "accordingly". Now that I and three levels of the DILG organization are all informed and guided, I am compelled to inquire as to what role and responsibility any of these other offices have with regard to applying your guidance to the facts that were specifically included in my original letters to the Ivisan ML GOO. I assume that this responsibility to decide the questions now falls to the MLGOO? And if the MLGOO is not responsible to apply the guidance to the facts, and to inform the Ivisan Sangguniang Bayan's presiding officer that he has

or has not acted appropriately, then what am I to do with the guidance? Do you expect me to present your opinion to the presiding officer? And if that is the case, do you feel that DILG has fulfilled its own mission statement? The following is the Vision and Mission statement, Goals and Objectives, and Quality Policy of DILG. In it, DILG pledges "provide effective technical and administrative services to promote excellence in local govemance... for the LGU's to become transparent, ..., socially protective, ... where people in the community live happily. Having provided the legal bases through that assailed legal opinion, it should have prompted an understanding that, relying thereon, if the concerned member of the Sanggunian identifies any irregularity of proceedings that may constitute a cause of action on his/her part, the intervention of the court may be sought, if necessary. If we may add to the ostensible need for explanation, the acts of legislative bodies enjoy the presumption of validity/regularity and constitutionality — the very reason why only courts of proper jurisdiction may declare assailed actions invalid/irregular or unconstitutional, not this Department. The Department, particularly the field offices of this Department that have been mentioned, should not be expected to intervene into matters that are internal to the proceedings of the Sanggunian- a local legislative body. Otherwise, the constitutionally granted principle of local autonomy of local government units will be violated outright. Having laid the foregoing premise, the Sangguniang Bayan Member of Ivisan, Capiz, Ms. Azucena Chapman, should be enlightened that the Department's exercise of its mandate of local government supervision while strictly observing the constitutional limitations, is in no way to be construed as a way of not fulfilling its mission statement. The Department and its field offices perform functions within the bounds of its delegated authority as much as it respects the local government officials' proper exercise of their functions and their implied responsibility to acquire basic knowledge incidental to the functions of their offices/positions they are appointed/elected to. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AU H RITY OF THE SECRETARY: DILG; Un e GAN, CESO Ill ry for Local Government

LLLS/84 Copy Furnished: DIR. JUAN JOVIAN E. INGENERO, CESO Office of the Provincial Director Office Of the MLGOO DILG Region VI DILG-Capiz Ivisan, Capiz 6 parola Street, Fort San Pedro, Iloilo City
